 This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order
Petitioner-accused No.29 who was working as Tahasildar along with other accused have been charge sheeted for the offence under Sections 143, 465, 468, 419, 420, 120B r/w Section 149 of IPC.

2. FIR was lodged by the 2nd respondent with the jurisdictional Police alleging that, Smt.
Chikkamma along with her seven children have fabricated documents to the effect that, they are the legal representatives of T. Siddappa, original owner of the subject property, and by using the fabricated documents submitted an application with the Revenue Inspector for mutating their names in the revenue records, and upon objection filed by the 2nd respondent, the Revenue Inspector referred the dispute to the Tahasildar, the Tahasildar after considering objections,
mutated the names of Smt. Chikkamma and her seven children as legal representatives of T.
Siddappa.
3. The cognizance taken of the aforesaid offence by the learned Magistrate is impugned in this petition by accused No.29.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner- accused No.29 submits that, mutating the names of Smt. Chikkamma and her seven children as legal representatives of the T. Siddappa in the revenue Chandra vs State Of Karnataka on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106823659/

sentences.text: Hence, in the absence of sanction to prosecute the petitioner-accused No.29 under Section 197 of Cr.P.C., the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is one without authority of law.

5. He further submits that, there was no allegation in the FIR that, the petitioner-accused No.29 connived with other accused in creating the document, and in the absence of any corroborative material, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is also impermissible.

6. On the other hand, learned HCGP appearing for the State would submit that, the charge sheet material discloses the commission of the offence alleged against the petitioner- accused No.29, and the veracity of the allegation can be considered after full fledged trial, and at this stage, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate does not warrant any interference.
7. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

8. Section 197 of Cr.P.C., specifies that, no Court shall take cognizance of any offence against the public servant, alleged to have been committed by him while acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty, except with the previous sanction of the Competent Authority.

9. In the instant case, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is without the previous order,
granting sanction to prosecute the petitioner-accused No.29 by the Competent Authority.
Hence, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate, in the absence of sanction stands vitiated.

10. In the FIR lodged by the 2nd respondent, there is no allegation that the petitioner-accused No.29 connived with the other accused in fabricating the document, and in the absence of any specific allegation much less the corroborative material, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate is also impermissible.
11. In view of the same, the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioner-accused No.29 will be an abuse of process of law.
Accordingly, I pass the following:

ORDER i) The Criminal petition is allowed;
ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.1577/2016, on the file of the Additional Civil Judge & JMFC, Doaddaballapura insofar it relates to the petitioner-accused No.29 is hereby quashed.
